description:
FILED s514f (Opus, 2026-10-11) while fixing #2920.  PRE-EXISTING on main 8f2fa11c.

A word this file DECLARES as a sub (no prototype), written in print's handle slot, is a CALL in perl and a FILEHANDLE in PCL -- SILENT WRONG:

    sub FOO {3} print FOO "x\n"; print "end\n";
perl 5.40.3: 3end   (FOO("x\n") is called; its value 3 is printed)
PCL:         end    (prints "x\n" to the never-opened handle FOO)

The `*` spelling `sub FOO {3} print FOO * 2, "\n"` (perl: FOO(*2, "\n") -> prints 3) is still a LOUD drop on purpose: #2920's glob repair is skipped for a declared sub so as not to turn it silent.  Fix site: PExpr's print filehandle decision (the bareword arm near `fh_bareword_shape`): a word `_bareword_callable_here` answers 'yes' for (declared above, no `()` prototype) is a call, not a handle, unless it is a registered filehandle (`open(FOO, ...)` wins).  Probe the lowercase spelling and a sub declared BELOW the print ('not-yet': perl reads the handle).
subject: a declared sub in print's handle slot is a CALL in perl, a filehandle in PCL (print FOO "x" with sub FOO) -- silent wrong
